title: I’m building a step up from Discord and Drive for small game dev teams
author: KaseyNorth
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’m the solo dev behind Wippack. I’m building it to help small teams manage their game assets when passing files around in Discord and Drive starts getting messy.

Things like:

* **“Which file is the latest?”** Models, textures, and other assets are scattered across messages, shared folders, and people’s computers.
* **Working on an outdated version** because someone missed an upload or grabbed the wrong file.
* **Wanting to undo a change** but not having an easy way to find the version from before.
* **Copying entire folders for milestones** and ending up with a pile of “final” and “final\_v2” backups.

With Wippack, you work from a folder on your computer and files sync to your team automatically. It keeps version history so you can restore older files, and save points let you capture a group of files together when you reach a milestone.

You can also browse and preview assets in your browser without downloading everything just to check what’s there.

I want it to feel familiar for teams already using shared folders, while making it easier to keep track of the work. I’d love feedback from other small teams on whether this would fit into how you make games.

replies.author: KaseyNorth
replies.body:
similar idea with version history, yeah.   
  
wippack is more like a shared asset folder that automatically syncs, keeps older versions, and lets you preview models and textures. git can store those too i'm just making that workflow easier for small teams without everyone needing to learn git
